A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Lavida-O research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite reformatting and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original understanding, generation, grounding and editing results, along with architectural ablations, sampling comparisons and efficiency experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds compositional-generation evaluations and a human preference study of universal text conditioning.

M1.justification: The Elastic-MoT architecture, modality-aware masking, conditioning, stratified sampling, coordinate quantization and training procedure are retained. Algorithm 3 documents the planning, feedback, stopping and history-truncation procedure already described in v1 Appendix A.7; it does not establish a new method.

E1.justification: v3 adds T2I-Compbench++ evaluations covering 3D relations, 2D relations and texture attribution (Table 14), extending compositional coverage beyond GenEval. Training datasets and existing benchmark coverage remain unchanged. The human study uses prompts from the already-used MJHQ-30k dataset.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 add Janus-Pro-1B and UniGen-1.5B comparisons. Table 5 removes ICEdit, previously reported with an overall score of 3.05. The new T2I-Compbench++ comparison includes Stable Diffusion 2, Janus-Pro-7B and FLUX.1 Dev; the remaining established comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix B.6 introduces a pairwise preference protocol with 300 human responses, randomly selected MJHQ-30k prompts, conditioning enabled versus disabled, and explicit judging instructions. Table 3 specifies SFT-stage results for the newly included UniGen comparison. Existing training configurations in Table 7 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 illustrates conditioning effects qualitatively in Figure 8; v3 adds a direct human preference ablation with and without conditioning. Appendix B.5 also extends the planning analysis to 3D relations and texture attribution. These are targeted additions to the retained architecture, sampling, data-pipeline and reflection analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed summaries, confidence intervals or formal significance tests for these results. The new human preference chart has no uncertainty estimates. Its 300 responses specify study sample size, rather than repeated model runs or an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark values match, including GenEval scores of 0.77/0.85/0.89. v3 adds comparator entries, one-step grounding split scores, human preferences and T2I-Compbench++ results. In the new planning comparison, 3D scores are 0.414 without planning and 0.442 with it. Table 4 identifies the former grounding row as four-step, so the additional one-step scores are not a same-setting decline. Several qualitative examples also change.

T1.justification: Following Equation 1, v3 corrects the factorization statement: the product of token probabilities represents p_theta(X0|Xt), whereas v1 incorrectly assigns that factorization to log p_theta(X0|Xt). The objective and Appendix A derivations otherwise remain unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the unified masked-diffusion model, efficient Elastic-MoT design, and planning/reflection that connect understanding with generation. The state-of-the-art performance and inference-efficiency claims retain their scope. The rewritten abstract emphasizes existing contributions rather than introducing a different scientific claim.

C2.justification: v3 explains the new 3D-planning results through object sizes that convey distance despite using 2D boxes. Appendix B.2 adds an optimization explanation for larger generation branches needing more training and tuning. The existing limitations concerning text rendering, pixel shift, reasoning and hallucination are substantively retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly states code/checkpoint availability and provides a repository address. It adds a planning prompt, reflection pseudocode, human-study instructions and an explicit four-step label for existing grounding results. Conversely, the shortened setup drops explicit aggregate counts, including v1's 12M Stage-1 and 3M interleaved samples. Hardware and detailed training configurations remain.

R1.justification: v3 expands positioning with X-Fusion, LM-Fusion and additional masked-diffusion work, and adds references supporting the new comparisons and benchmark. The ICEdit reference disappears. The new UMDD discussion is internally mismatched: Section 2.2 presents it as a unified MDM, but its bibliography entry concerns software development in 2008.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the abstract, condenses related-work, method and setup passages, and combines the four task-specific results subsections under Main Results. It also changes the title/header, edits wording and adds an LLM-usage appendix. The overall narrative and section sequence remain recognizable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the T2I-Compbench++ table, human-preference chart and reflection algorithm box; revises comparison-table rows; and replaces selected introductory and gallery examples. Conference formatting changes spacing, headings and placements. Existing architecture diagrams and efficiency plots are retained, while later figures and tables are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The conditioning preference study and additional planning evaluations provide useful evidence for existing design choices. The repository information, reflection pseudocode and explicit grounding step counts also improve documentation. These incremental gains outweigh limited regressions, including omitted training-data totals and the mismatched UMDD citation. Sparse human-study details and absent uncertainty estimates limit the strength of the added evidence; the core method and established results remain unchanged.
